headline: Sleep debt is today's driver — protect tonight's sleep before tomorrow's tempo run.
body_state: The deterministic call is red, driven by sleep: 26h of 14-day sleep debt and only 6.3h last night (score 66 — 2h deep, 4h light, 18min REM). HRV 45ms is BALANCED and skin temp is -0.7°C (no illness flag), so this isn't an overtraining or sickness signal, just accumulated sleep debt. Body battery started the day at 47 after a solid +43 overnight recharge; resting HR 48, stress avg a calm 17. Training status reads "Recovery," TSB -10.5 on CTL 36 — a normal, digesting-load state, not a crisis.
session: No running-plan workout was scheduled today — the Base block's first session (4km tempo) starts tomorrow. This morning's Un1t class is already done (06:06, 46min, RPE 7, 53% of the time in Z4, no cool-down tail on the HR trace). Given the sleep-debt call, don't add more load today: let the Un1t effort stand as the day's stimulus and spend the evening on recovery, not more training. Tomorrow's 4km tempo (10min easy @ 4:50-5:19/km → 4km threshold @ 4:18-4:32/km → 10min easy) needs you rested — go to bed ~60 min earlier tonight so it isn't run on today's debt.
recent: The last four days show the grey-zone pattern that's your #1 ranked limiter (only 17.8% easy running vs an 80% target). Aug 7's progressive long run closed at 179bpm/RPE8 instead of easy, dropping readiness to 23 the next day. Aug 8's Un1t class (TE 2.8/2.1) went unrated. Aug 10's "5km Easy Run" spent 89.7% of its time in zone 3 at 4:27/km — not easy — with cadence still low at 157.6spm. Today's Un1t repeated the pattern: hard (53% Z4) with no taper-down. Four moderate-to-hard days in a row is exactly why easy-day intensity, not volume, is the thing to fix.
focus: Protect sleep tonight — bed ~60 min earlier is the single biggest lever on today's red call.
Tomorrow's tempo: make the warm-up/cool-down genuinely easy (HR 115-130, not 4:20s/km) so the 4km threshold segment gets a fair, fresh test.
Keep chasing the grey-zone fix — this week's easy days and Un1t classes have all run moderate-to-hard; dial the effort back on days that aren't meant to be quality.
